findings.reason: the plan must either normalise both sides through the one `section_record_id` derivation or state that declaration keys are already normalised, which they are not; without it §16's stated "one producer of identity" invariant is broken at the exact join it exists to serve.
findings.text: `implementable_sections` returns the raw authored declaration key (`str(raw_section).strip()`, so a plan id authored `s5.1` yields `s5.1`), while §16 keys `_section_digests` through `section_record_id`, which normalises `s5.1` to `s5-1` (routing.py:215-226). §18 fixes the coverage predicate on `implementable_sections` unchanged and §16 joins its output to the digest keys, so for any plan carrying a dotted section id — and `docs/plans/crew-effort-routing.html` and `docs/plans/self-hosted-worker-backends.html` carry `s1.1`…`s11.6` today — the outstanding section and its stored digest never compare equal, and the gate composes a fresh review on every dispatch of a section that is in fact covered.

findings.reason: the plan should name these two inline sites and converge them on the hoisted derivation (or extend the census rule to report inline heading-identity expressions), otherwise §17 lands the derivation beside a fork of itself.
findings.text: the file §17 designates as the home of the hoisted identity derivation already derives section identity by a rule of its own, twice: `_read_section_records` takes `element.get("id","")` for an h2 and `element.get("data-id","")` for a section (386-389), and `_splice_section_records` repeats the same expression at 861; both hand back the raw element id, so `s5.1` stays `s5.1` where `section_record_id` would return `s5-1`. §17's done-when instrument (the thirteen-name grep, the no-import-from-store grep, the moved-name importer grep, `def landed_section_ids`) looks for named helpers and imports and cannot see either inline expression, so the section can pass its gate with three identity rules co-resident in the file it calls identity's owner.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 hides heading enumeration, identity, level, span and card recognition behind one parser with one public reader (`plan_headings`); §16 hides the prose bucketing, the section-set digest and the coverage join behind one private function each, and the interface is smaller than the behaviour behind it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 joins `roadmap.implementable_sections` to its new section digests across two different spellings of one identity.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 is the only section adding a public definition and names what moves in its place (`landed_section_ids` re-homed under the same name, net one), while §16 and §18 state in their own text that nothing is added or retired.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism the design names (the span parser, the store's twelve heading/card helpers, the interface-count census, the four §18 readers, the two c-run- owners) was opened in the tree and exists where the plan says; the plan searched before proposing.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 states why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (it joins an outstanding set to a union of digests, adding no walk of its own) and §17 extends the existing parser rather than layering a scanner over it, so neither the predicate nor `plan_headings` is an unjustified thin layer.
